title: Tuning temperature, top-k and top-p to the task

videos.script: Before a model writes a token, it gives every token it could write a score. A separate step, the sampler, picks one. {{title}} Here is a customer asking whether they can pay with a gift card and a credit card together. A person labelled it billing. The model gives other sixty-two percent, billing twenty-two, and a little to tokens that would break the label check: billing with a capital, billing with a space in front. {{scores}} Divide the scores by a low temperature and almost every draw is the top token. Raise it, and the tail wakes up. Shipping and payment, which are not labels at all, get drawn. {{temperature}} Top-k and top-p cut that tail off before the draw. One keeps a fixed number of tokens. The other keeps a share of the probability. {{cut}} Then the triage prompt, five calls per message. At temperature zero, all five agree. At temperature one, the categories hold, and fifteen urgencies turn wrong. Sampling found the close calls. {{task}} By the end of this lesson you can read a sampling setting as arithmetic. You can choose one for the task in front of you. And you can say why zero is still not a promise from one machine to the next. {{close}}
